newsitem.title: USA: US Rep English would increase IDB volume cap.
newsitem.headline: US Rep English would increase IDB volume cap.

text.p: U.S. Rep Phil English introduced two bills designed to ease restrictions on the amount of industrial development bonds (IDBs) that states and localities can issue on a tax-exempt basis.

One measure, H.R. 840, would raise the total dollar amount of IDBs that localities can issue on a tax-exempt basis, called the volume cap, from the current $10 million to $20 million, an to English said in a telephone interview.

A second measure, H.R. 842, would permit small-issue IDB offerings to be "bank qualified." That means that banks could deduct up to 80 percent of the interest they pay to finance small-issue IDBs, the aide said.

The provision would apply to bond offerings under $5 million, the aide said. English's bill also would give states and localities a clearer definition of what types of local manufacturing projects would qualify for IDB financing.
And the measure would increase the current cap on the volume of IDBs that a locality can issue from $50 to $75 per capita, the aide said.
English is a Republican from Pennsylvania. He introduced the legislation late Wednesday.
